mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST for two consecutive months indicates weakening consumer spending and housing demand, which reduces corporate revenue and confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.75 percentage points in a single month, combined with a concurrent increase in CPIAUCSL above 3%, signals aggressive tightening and inflation risk, which erodes equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps > 0.75% in one month AND CPIAUCSL > 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals rising household savings, which often coincides with precautionary behavior and reduced consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
